fields.title: Who signs and what they fear
fields.keyTakeaway: An objection is a voiced risk, not an argument. Responding to it with a feature list is useless: the person signing the contract risks their reputation, and that is the risk you need to address.
fields.checkQuestion: Is "too expensive" from the business owner the same objection as "too expensive" from the warehouse manager?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **what arguments and counterarguments to use?** The answer depends not on the product, but on who is in front of you and what they stand to lose.
fields.blocks/1/text: Kedr is a fictional cloud warehouse management service for small distributors: receiving, putaway, dispatch. Sold through a sales team, average check is 40 thousand rubles a month, deal cycle is about two months. We will return to it in every lesson in this domain.
fields.blocks/2/text: **What happens if you do not answer the question.** The salesperson responds to any objection with a feature walkthrough. The client politely agrees and takes time "to think," never returning.
fields.blocks/3/subtitle: A portrait of the decision-maker, not the user
fields.blocks/3/items/0: **Role in the decision** — who initiates, who approves, who can block. Often three different people.
fields.blocks/3/items/1: **What success means to them** — how they are evaluated at their job.
fields.blocks/3/items/2: **What they risk by saying "yes"** — this is where almost all objections live.
fields.blocks/3/items/3: **Who they have to justify it to** — the decision is almost always pitched to someone else.
fields.blocks/4/text: A Buyer Persona is not the same as a user persona. A user evaluates convenience; a buyer evaluates risk. Everyone in the warehouse might love the product, yet it will not sell because the warehouse does not sign the deal.
fields.blocks/5/items/0: "Too expensive" from the owner — "I do not understand what I get for this money": needs an ROI calculation
fields.blocks/5/items/1: "Too expensive" from the warehouse manager — "they will cut my other budget": needs a discussion on trade-offs
fields.blocks/5/items/2: "I need to consult" — almost always "I have nothing to justify this decision to my boss": needs leave-behind materials
fields.blocks/5/items/3: "Everything works fine for us" — "switching costs more than the problem": needs a switching cost estimate, not a feature list
fields.blocks/6/text:
Warehouse manager at a demo: "We do not have time for implementation."

The salesperson kept replying that onboarding takes two weeks and that we configure everything ourselves. The deal stalled for a month.

On the fourth meeting, the real issue surfaced: his risk was that warehouse operations would halt during transition, and he would be held responsible. Whether it takes two weeks or four does not matter; what matters is what happens if something goes wrong.

The deal moved forward when we offered to run in parallel with the old system for the first month. Not a single new feature was needed for this.
fields.blocks/7/text: A persona is a generalization, and a real person is always different. It is useful for prep work and harmful if used to make assumptions instead of asking questions. Also, it describes the purchase decision, not renewal: renewals involve different people and different risks.
